title: Right derivation preserves strict cyclic presentations
statement: Let C and D be Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], F and G additive autoequivalences with their fixed-pair categories [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category], and use chosen ordinary derived categories in independent morphism universes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let L:C→D be additive left exact, and e:L⋙G≅F⋙L. Let hF and hC be arbitrary witnesses that every complex in C^F, respectively C, admits a quasi-isomorphism into a K-injective complex. Write J=R(mapOfNatIso e) and H=RL for the recorded universal right-derived functors [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], and alpha=cyclicDerivedRightForgetComparison for the unique unit-normalized comparison of [def-sf-cyclic-derived-hom-data]. Equip H with any coherent integer-shift structure for which its recorded computation unit commutes with shifts. Write tr for cyclicDerivedHomTransport with this structure and alpha. For any M,N in D(C^F), u in V^{-1}(M,N) and f:M→N, every strict off-diagonal presentation of (u,f) [lem-sf-cyclic-derived-off-diagonal-presentation] gives a strict off-diagonal presentation of (tr(u),J(f)) in D(D^G). The representing extension may change. No boundedness or normalized boundary family is assumed.

proof.text: Use [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence] in the Grothendieck fixed-pair category to choose K-injective models J0 of M and A of N[-1] with injective terms. Forgetting preserves K-injectives by [lem-sf-fixed-pair-derived-forget-comparison]. The K-injective Hom bijection [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents the prescribed shifted underlying morphism by a chain map UJ0→UA.

proof.text: Construct the strict triangular extension A→E→J0 with this off-diagonal chain map using [lem-sf-cyclic-derived-off-diagonal-presentation]. Each inclusion A^n→E^n splits by injectivity of A^n. Thus the extension is degreewise split in the fixed-pair category. Its homotopy triangle shows E and the inclusion cone are K-injective because K-injectives form the triangulated right orthogonal of acyclics [lem-sf-kinjective-replacement-triangulated]. The canonical cone projection q to J0 is a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle], hence a homotopy equivalence by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Presentation uniqueness identifies the given f with the transported connecting morphism of this new extension.

proof.text: On A,E,J0 and the cone, the unit of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] is invertible. Termwise additivity preserves the degreewise splitting and the homotopy inverse of q, so the image sequence is short exact even without exactness of L on arbitrary sequences. The signed cone formula delta=-p q^{-1} of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] is therefore preserved, with the same sign.

proof.text: The unit equation for [lem-sf-fixed-pair-derived-forget-comparison] identifies both underlying models with L(UI). The assumed shift equation for the unit identifies the shifted class. Naturality of e at u0 turns L(F(u0) theta_A)e into G(L(u0)) times the new diagonal structure. Thus the image underlying chain splitting and off-diagonal map satisfy the target presentation equation of [def-sf-cyclic-derived-hom-data]. Use the images of the model isomorphisms and the unit-compatible shift to obtain its endpoint isomorphisms. The preserved signed cone formula supplies the native-morphism equation. This proves the target presentation without imposing boundedness.

theorem cyclicDerivedOffDiagonalPresentation_mapRightDerived
    {M N : DerivedCategory (IsoAlgebra F)} {u : CyclicDerivedHom F M N (-1)}
    {f : M ⟶ N} (hp : CyclicDerivedOffDiagonalPresentation F u f) :
    CyclicDerivedOffDiagonalPresentation G
      (cyclicDerivedHomTransport F G
        ((mapOfNatIso e).rightDerivedFunctorOfQuasiIsoResolutions hF)
        (L.rightDerivedFunctorOfQuasiIsoResolutions hC)
        (fun r ↦ (L.rightDerivedFunctorOfQuasiIsoResolutions hC).commShiftIso r)
        (cyclicDerivedRightForgetComparison F G L e hF hC) M N (-1) u)
      (((mapOfNatIso e).rightDerivedFunctorOfQuasiIsoResolutions hF).map f)
